reviews.summary: All three round-1 issues verified fixed, each checked rather than accepted. Issue 1: generated/leastttftjoint/{cmd,pkg} materialised, all 36 declared paths byte-identical to the checkout, no strays, shipped runner.go is the current 75-insertion version rather than v3's. Issue 2: the widening to a 35-path union across both manifests is endorsed as the better fix -- the reviewer's own prescription was insufficient and adding arm.go plus evalfixture.go alone only rotated the failure. The union is checkable in one line rather than argued: for BOTH manifests the declared set (35 files_created plus runner.go) equals EXACTLY the git-dirty set at 36 paths, so restore_baseline from either manifest returns the tree to pristine HEAD with nothing stranded in either direction, and both generated trees being 36/36 identical to the checkout makes them byte-identical to each other so materialising in either order is idempotent. The narrower alternative was rejected because 'only the leastttftjoint manifest may be used for baseline toggling' is an undeclared precondition, the class of silent constraint the pipeline exists to remove. Issue 3: the corrected producer paragraph is accurate and states the named consequence, and the reviewer verified the new test's teeth itself by two independent perturbations of the shipped overlay, restoring it byte-identical by sha256 -- changing this arm's token-producer vllm.url fails at overlay_test.go:348 and removing approx-prefix-cache-producer fails at :342, so both branches are live and producerEntry unmarshals parameters so key order cannot mask an inequality. Criteria: fidelity confirmed operand for operand against algorithms/least_ttft_joint.go with divergence limited to the three declared items and identity structural rather than maintained; code quality confirmed with 39 tests in this package and the cross-arm binding guard closing a real silent-arm-swap; registration confirmed with three-arg Register at StabilityBeta and the picker via RegisterWithPluginDependencies; core modification declared with reason and upstream-rebase risk; config, assembly and treatment config all confirmed, both coefficient sets matching config.md section 4 to the last digit. FOCAL BEHAVIOUR PRESERVATION verified independently against the pre-refactor snapshot: 188 test functions before and after with an identical sorted name list, all 188 pass, and each production change reduces to a no-op for an objective whose ReadsSLOValueConfig() is true. Sharing Config upheld on the reviewer's own reasoning, with the confirmation that the specification's SECOND named prohibition (NomPrefillTokens) is enforced via the capacity block rather than by name -- now documented. One item explicitly NOT this arm's and flagged to the team lead: the focal manifest's description field still does not mention arm.go, evalfixture.go, Objective, the seam, the union, or this arm, so that arm's declaration does not yet describe the tree it ships. It does not gate this arm. APPROVE RE-CONFIRMED ON v6 after the NomPrefillTokens clause landed, verified rather than assumed safe: v5->v6 touched exactly one file, causalsloexternality/config.go, and stripping comments and blank lines from both snapshots produces an identical file, so no code line changed in the already-approved focal package. The clause's non-obvious half was checked at source -- muDNom and muPNom are reached only from capacity.go:79 and :83 while the admission contexts use muDecode and muPrefill at policy.go:378 and :403, which read only batch state, so with capacity not live for this arm neither nominal-rate method is ever called and the specification's stated reason holds as written. NO STALE-TREE REGRESSION: both generated trees carry the new config.go at 36/36 byte-identical with zero strays, and for both manifests the declared set still equals exactly the git-dirty set -- a comment-only edit to a shared production file being precisely the change that could quietly re-open issue 2. Gates green on v6 with focal 188 PASS and comparator 39 PASS. Fidelity unaffected: rounds 2 and the v6 edit changed no production logic anywhere (objective.go and evalfixture.go comment-only at v5, config.go comment-only at v6, plus one test assertion), so the round-1 fidelity verification stands without re-derivation. The reviewer also escalated the copy_generated precondition to the team lead with a one-line acceptance test: after any regeneration, each manifest's declared set must equal the git-dirty set exactly.
